question: How many months of unprotected intercourse define clinical infertility in standard health guidelines?
explanation: Clinical guidelines define infertility as failing to achieve pregnancy after one full year of regular unprotected intercourse. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in reproductive health?

options.A: Managing chronic hormonal disorders in adults
options.D: Stopping reproductive health issues before they start

explanation: Primary prevention stops health problems from occurring in the first place through education and protective measures. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h1)

question: How does tobacco smoking mainly cause infertility in reproductive cells?

options.A: Elevating systemic blood pressure in the pelvis
options.B: Accelerating oocyte depletion and damaging sperm DNA
options.C: Causing permanent blockage of the vas deferens
options.D: Increasing the thickness of the cervical mucus

explanation: Chemicals in tobacco smoke are toxic to reproductive cells, leading to faster egg loss in women and genetic damage in sperm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: A female patient with a body mass index of 38 struggles to conceive. What is the main hormonal reason for this?

options.A: Excess adipose tissue alters estrogen metabolism and stops ovulation
options.B: Increased thyroid hormone blocks the release of mature eggs
options.C: High muscle mass suppresses the normal function of the pituitary gland
options.D: Low body fat completely halts the production of progesterone

explanation: Obesity impacts hormone balance, frequently resulting in cycles without ovulation that prevent pregnancy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h2)

question: Which two bacterial pathogens are most commonly linked to tubal factor infertility?

options.B: Human papillomavirus and Herpes simplex virus

explanation: These specific bacteria cause silent upper reproductive tract infections that lead to tubal scarring. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: Why do chlamydial infections often cause severe pelvic inflammatory disease before they are noticed?

options.A: The pathogen attacks the immune system directly instead of reproductive organs
options.B: The bacteria destroy all local nerve endings so the patient feels no pain
options.C: The infection often presents with very few or no noticeable symptoms
options.D: Antibiotic resistance develops rapidly before standard tests can identify it

explanation: Asymptomatic infections allow bacteria to travel upward into the fallopian tubes without prompting early medical care. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h3)

question: Industrial workers handling which toxic metals face a high risk of altered reproductive hormones?
explanation: Heavy metals like lead and mercury are known reproductive toxins that disrupt endocrine function. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: A radiographer who forgets to wear a lead apron is concerned about childbearing. What is the main physiological risk?

options.A: Cumulative cellular damage to developing gametes
options.B: Rapid weight gain from radiation-induced metabolic slowing
options.C: Sudden cessation of pituitary hormone secretion
options.D: Permanent blockage of the uterine arteries

explanation: Chronic ionizing radiation harms cellular DNA in both eggs and sperm, threatening reproductive viability. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h4)

question: What is the main feature of endometriosis that threatens a woman's fertility?

options.A: Enlargement of the cervix blocking normal sperm entry
options.B: Presence of endometrial tissue outside the uterus causing adhesions
options.C: Complete absence of the fallopian tubes from birth
options.D: Overproduction of insulin by the pancreas damaging the ovaries

explanation: Endometrial tissue outside the uterus creates inflammation and scar tissue that distorts pelvic structures. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: How does polycystic ovary syndrome directly interfere with a woman's ability to conceive?

options.A: By causing irregular menstrual cycles and absent ovulation
options.B: By producing thick cervical mucus that destroys all sperm
options.C: By accelerating the complete depletion of all eggs by age twenty
options.D: By shrinking the uterus so an embryo cannot implant

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome disrupts normal hormone feedback loops, frequently preventing the release of eggs. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why is it important to evaluate both partners during an infertility assessment?

options.A: Men are always the primary cause of unfulfilled reproductive plans
options.B: Female patients refuse to speak with healthcare providers alone
options.C: Infertility factors can originate from male partners, female partners, or both
options.D: Insurance companies refuse to pay for individual diagnostic assessments

explanation: Because reproductive challenges involve both biological sexes equally, evaluating both partners ensures an accurate diagnosis. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)

question: Which quality is most important for a nurse providing reproductive health counseling?

options.A: A non-judgmental approach and active listening
options.B: Immediate prescription of advanced fertility drugs
options.C: Strict adherence to rigid personal moral beliefs
options.D: Focusing exclusively on the female partner's history

explanation: Creating a safe, open environment encourages patients to share sensitive lifestyle and health details. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T22#GNS312_U1_T22_h6)
